security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from fenced command examples in a local Kubernetes guide. One real concern remains: the skill documents a sudo /etc/hosts modification, and it also includes placeholder secret examples that users should not copy into real environments.

remediation.issue: Privileged host-file modification is shown as a normal access step.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before running the sudo /etc/hosts command and offer safer alternatives such as minikube service, port-forwarding, or manually reviewing the hosts entry.

remediation.issue: Examples include literal Kubernetes secret values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace literal password examples with placeholders and explain that real secrets should come from a secret manager or local-only test values.

content.value_statement: Local Kubernetes setup can be slow when teams need repeatable Minikube commands and manifests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused guide for local clusters, images, services, and debugging.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to start, stop, and configure Minikube clusters for local development.
Lists kubectl commands for contexts, pods, logs, events, rollouts, and resource inspection.
Shows how to build local Docker images for Minikube and use imagePullPolicy settings.
Provides example Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, and Ingress manifests.
Guides local service access through NodePort, LoadBalancer tunnel, port forwarding, and ingress.
Includes troubleshooting commands for pod startup, crashes, networking, and resource usage.
limitations: It focuses on local Minikube workflows, not production cluster operations.
It does not automate commands; users or agents must review commands before execution.
It uses placeholder names and manifests that require adaptation for real applications.
It does not replace Kubernetes security review, policy validation, or cluster hardening.

use_cases.title: Set up a local cluster
use_cases.description: Create a Minikube environment with useful addons and enough resources for development testing.

use_cases.title: Debug a failing workload
use_cases.description: Use kubectl logs, describe, events, exec, and resource metrics to investigate local pod failures.

use_cases.title: Prepare local Kubernetes manifests
use_cases.description: Draft basic Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, and Ingress examples for a local app.

prompt_templates.title: Start a local cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me start a Minikube cluster for local development with ingress and metrics enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a local image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to guide me through building a Docker image into Minikube and deploying it with Kubernetes manifests.

prompt_templates.title: Debug pod failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose why my local Kubernetes pod is not starting and list the kubectl checks in order.

prompt_templates.title: Review local access options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare NodePort, minikube tunnel, port-forwarding, and ingress for accessing my local service.

output_examples.input: Help me run a web app in local Kubernetes.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines Minikube startup, addon setup, image building, manifest application, and service access steps.

output_examples.input: My pod keeps crashing in Minikube.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests checking pod events, previous container logs, resource usage, and network dependencies in a safe order.

output_examples.input: I need an ingress-based local development flow.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains enabling ingress, applying an ingress manifest, and reviewing any host-file change before using elevated privileges.

best_practices: Review every command before execution, especially commands that use sudo or modify host configuration.
Use placeholder manifests as learning examples and adapt names, images, ports, and resource settings to your app.
Keep local-only secrets separate from real credentials and avoid copying sample passwords into shared files.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged host-file changes without confirming the exact entry being added.
Do not treat local Minikube settings as production Kubernetes guidance.
Do not paste real passwords into command history or sample Secret manifests.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Kubernetes cluster automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and guidance that a user or agent can review and run.

faq.question: Is this skill for production Kubernetes?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for local development and testing with Minikube.

faq.question: Can it help with kubectl debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands for logs, events, pod descriptions, exec sessions, and resource checks.

faq.question: Does it support local Docker images?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to build images for Minikube and set local image pull behavior.

faq.question: Why does the audit mention sudo?
faq.answer: One ingress example edits /etc/hosts with sudo. Users should review that command before running it.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
